note: WAEC English Paper 3 (Test of Orals) round 1: phonetics items in CBT multiple-choice form.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel /iː/?
questions.explanation: Sheep is pronounced /ʃiːp/ with the long /iː/; ship has /ɪ/, shop /ɒ/ and soap /əʊ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel /ɪ/?
questions.explanation: Sit is /sɪt/; seat has /iː/, set /e/ and sat /æ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'e' pronounced /e/?
questions.explanation: Bed is /bed/ with /e/; beat is /biːt/, bite /baɪt/ and boot /buːt/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel /æ/?
questions.explanation: Cat is /kæt/ with /æ/; cot /kɒt/, coat /kəʊt/ and cut /kʌt/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'o' pronounced /ɒ/?
questions.explanation: Hot is /hɒt/; the other three words all contain the diphthong /əʊ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel /ɔː/?
questions.explanation: Four is /fɔː/; five is /faɪv/, fire /ˈfaɪə/ and file /faɪl/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'u' pronounced /ʌ/?
questions.explanation: Cup is /kʌp/; cool is /kuːl/, cube /kjuːb/ and cute /kjuːt/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel /ʊ/?
questions.explanation: Book is /bʊk/ with short /ʊ/; boot is /buːt/, blue /bluː/ and move /muːv/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the letter combination 'oo' pronounced /uː/?
questions.explanation: Food is /fuːd/ with long /uː/; book /bʊk/, full /fʊl/ and put /pʊt/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel /ɑː/?
questions.explanation: Car is /kɑː/; cat /kæt/, coat /kəʊt/ and cure /kjʊə/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the vowel /ɜː/ found?
questions.explanation: Bird is /bɜːd/; bear /beə/, bare /beə/ and bar /bɑː/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word does the unstressed vowel /ə/ (schwa) appear at the start?
questions.explanation: About is /əˈbaʊt/ and opens with the schwa /ə/; the others have /uː/, /iː/ and /iː/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the diphthong /eɪ/?
questions.explanation: Face is /feɪs/ with /eɪ/; foot /fʊt/, moon /muːn/ and book /bʊk/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the letter combination 'ie' pronounced /aɪ/?
questions.explanation: Five is /faɪv/ with /aɪ/ for 'ie'; in field the 'ie' is /iː/, while fire and find do not use 'ie' that way.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the diphthong /ɔɪ/?
questions.explanation: Choice is /tʃɔɪs/ with /ɔɪ/; chair /tʃeə/, cheer /tʃɪə/ and cheap /tʃiːp/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the letter combination 'ou' pronounced /aʊ/?
questions.explanation: House is /haʊs/ with /aʊ/; though /ðəʊ/, through /θruː/ and group /gruːp/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the diphthong /əʊ/?
questions.explanation: Phone is /fəʊn/ with /əʊ/; the other words all have the long /uː/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is the letter combination 'air' pronounced /eə/?
questions.explanation: Chair is /tʃeə/; fear /fɪə/, near /nɪə/ and hear /hɪə/ all use /ɪə/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which pair of words both contain the diphthong /aʊ/?
questions.explanation: Mouth /maʊθ/ and south /saʊθ/ both use /aʊ/; the other pairs use different vowels.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is 'ough' pronounced /uː/?
questions.explanation: Through is /θruː/; though is /ðəʊ/, thought /θɔːt/ and cough /kɒf/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is 'ough' pronounced /əʊ/?
questions.explanation: Though is /ðəʊ/; through is /θruː/, thought /θɔːt/ and cough /kɒf/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is 'ough' pronounced /ɔː/?
questions.explanation: Thought is /θɔːt/ with /ɔː/; though /ðəʊ/, through /θruː/ and cough /kɒf/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word is 'ough' pronounced /ɒ/?
questions.explanation: Cough is /kɒf/; though /ðəʊ/, through /θruː/ and bough /baʊ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which pair of words has the same vowel sound?
questions.explanation: Sheep /ʃiːp/ and beat /biːt/ both have /iː/; the other pairs differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which of the following words begins with the sound /θ/?
questions.explanation: Think begins with voiceless /θ/; this, that and they all begin with /ð/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is 'th' pronounced /ð/?
questions.explanation: That is /ðæt/; think /θɪŋk/, three /θriː/ and thick /θɪk/ use voiceless /θ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which of the following words contains the sound /ʃ/?
questions.explanation: Sugar is /ˈʃʊɡə/ with /ʃ/; the other words begin with /s/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the letter 's' pronounced /ʒ/?
questions.explanation: In measure the 's' is voiced as /ʒ/ (/meʒə/); in the others it is /s/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which of the following words ends with the sound /tʃ/?
questions.explanation: Watch is /wɒtʃ/ and ends in /tʃ/; the other words end in /eə/, /iː/ and /iːp/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is 'ch' pronounced /k/?
questions.explanation: In school, 'ch' is /k/ (/skuːl/); in the others it is /tʃ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'c' pronounced /s/?
questions.explanation: City is /ˈsɪti/; in car, cake and cool the 'c' is /k/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which word ends with the sound /ŋ/?
questions.explanation: Singing ends in the nasal /ŋ/; sing ends in /g/, sings in /z/ and singer in /ə/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is 'x' pronounced /ks/?
questions.explanation: Box ends in /ks/; in exam, exit and exact the 'x' is /z/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is 'x' pronounced /z/?
questions.explanation: Exam has /z/ for 'x' (/ɪɡzæm/); box, mix and fix all have /ks/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'k' silent?
questions.explanation: Knife is /naɪf/; the 'k' before 'n' is silent, as in knife, knee and knuckle.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'w' silent?
questions.explanation: Write is /raɪt/; the 'w' is silent in write, wrong and wrap.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the first 'h' silent?
questions.explanation: Hour is /aʊə/ with a silent 'h'; the others are pronounced with /h/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which pair of words begins with the sound /ʃ/?
questions.explanation: Ship /ʃɪp/ and sheep /ʃiːp/ both begin with /ʃ/; school begins /sk/, and the s-words begin with /s/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is 'ph' pronounced /f/ in the middle of the word?
questions.explanation: Graph /ɡrɑːf/ has /f/ for 'ph' in the middle; the others begin with /f/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'caught'?
questions.explanation: Caught /kɔːt/ and taught /tɔːt/ rhyme; catch /kætʃ/, coat /kəʊt/ and city do not.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'night'?
questions.explanation: Night /naɪt/ rhymes with light /laɪt/; knee /niː/, knew /njuː/ and coat /kəʊt/ do not.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'house'?
questions.explanation: House /haʊs/ rhymes with mouse /maʊs/; nose /nəʊz/, moose /muːs/ and rose /rəʊz/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'fire'?
questions.explanation: Fire /ˈfaɪə/ rhymes with tire /ˈtaɪə/; fur /fɜː/, four /fɔː/ and fair /feə/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'city'?
questions.explanation: City /ˈsɪti/ rhymes with pretty /ˈprɪti/; sitting /ˈsɪtɪŋ/, sister /ˈsɪstə/ and sit /sɪt/ do not.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'silly'?
questions.explanation: Silly /ˈsɪli/ rhymes with billy /ˈbɪli/; honey /ˈhni/, handy /ˈhændi/ and hilly /ˈhɪli/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'peach'?
questions.explanation: Peach /piːtʃ/ rhymes with beach /biːtʃ/; rich /rɪtʃ/, pitch /pɪtʃ/ and match /mætʃ/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'book'?
questions.explanation: Book /bʊk/ rhymes with look /lʊk/; back /bæk/, bag /bæg/ and bed /bed/ do not.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'came'?
questions.explanation: Came /keɪm/ rhymes with name /neɪm/; time /taɪm/, team /tiːm/ and home /həʊm/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'heart'?
questions.explanation: Heart /hɑːt/ rhymes with start /stɑːt/; hurt /hɜːt/, hair /heə/ and care /keə/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'shoe'?
questions.explanation: Shoe /ʃuː/ rhymes with blue /bluː/; shook /ʃʊk/, shake /ʃeɪk/ and short /ʃɔt/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'time'?
questions.explanation: Time /taɪm/ rhymes with crime /kraɪm/; team /tiːm/, home /həʊm/ and name /neɪm/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'question'?
questions.explanation: Question /ˈkwestʃən/ shares its /-ʃən/ ending with education /ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃən/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Rhymes
questions.q: Which pair of words rhymes?
questions.explanation: Caught /kɔːt/ and taught /tɔːt/ rhyme; the other pairs use different vowel sounds.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which word is the stress on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: Begin is /bɪˈɡɪn/ with second-syllable stress; teacher, garden and happy are stressed on the first.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which of these words is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: Hotel is /həʊˈtel/ with second-syllable stress; the others open with the stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which word does the stress fall on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: Machine is /məˈʃiːn/ with second-syllable stress; the others are first-syllable words.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which of the following words carries the stress on its second syllable?
questions.explanation: Descend is /dɪˈsend/ with second-syllable stress; the others carry first-syllable stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which word below has the stress on its SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: Arrive is /əˈraɪv/ with second-syllable stress; the others are stressed on the first.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: As a noun, which of these words is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: The noun permit is /pəˈmɪt/ with second-syllable stress; the others are first-syllable words.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which of the words below is the main stress on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: Explain is /ɪkˈspleɪn/ with second-syllable stress; the others are first-syllable words.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which word below is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: Deserve is /dɪˈzɜːv/ with second-syllable stress; the others open with the stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which word is the stress on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: Teacher is /ˈtiːtʃə/ with first-syllable stress; machine, hotel and begin are stressed later.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which of these words is stressed on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: Garden is /ˈɡɑːdn/ with first-syllable stress; the others carry second-syllable stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which word does the stress fall on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: English is /ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/ with first-syllable stress; the others are stressed on the second.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which word below carries the stress on its first syllable?
questions.explanation: Happy is /ˈhæpi/ with first-syllable stress; the others carry second-syllable stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which word is the main stress on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: Monday is /ˈmʌndeɪ/ with first-syllable stress; arrive, descend and relax are stressed later.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which word is the stress on the THIRD syllable?
questions.explanation: Vegetable is /ˌvedʒəˈteɪbəl/ with the main stress on the third syllable /teɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which of these words is stressed on the THIRD syllable?
questions.explanation: Information is /ˌɪnfəmeɪʃn/ with the main stress on the third syllable /meɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which word does the stress fall on the THIRD syllable?
questions.explanation: Education is /ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃn/ with the main stress on the third syllable /keɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: As a noun, the word 'record' is stressed on which syllable?
questions.explanation: The noun REcord /ˈrekɔːd/ carries the stress on the first syllable; the verb reCORD falls on the second.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In which pair does the stress change between the noun and the verb?
questions.explanation: The noun PREsent /ˈpreznt/ and the verb preSENT /prɪˈzent/ have different stress positions.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: Which of these noun-verb pairs shows a change of stress?
questions.explanation: The noun CONtract /ˈkɒntrækt/ and the verb conTRACT /kənˈtrækt/ differ in stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Stress
questions.q: In compound nouns such as 'blackboard', the stress usually falls on
questions.explanation: Compound nouns like BLAckboard /ˈblækbɔːd/ carry the stress on their first part.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: What intonation do we use in the statement 'The examination will start at eight o'clock'?
questions.explanation: Statements end with a falling intonation, which signals a complete thought.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: What intonation do we use in the question 'Are you coming to the party'?
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions take a rising intonation at the end.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: What intonation do we use in the question 'Where did you buy the book'?
questions.explanation: Wh- questions (where, what, why) take a falling intonation, unlike yes/no questions.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: We use a RISING intonation in all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Commands such as 'Close the door' end with falling intonation; the others commonly rise.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: In the list 'I bought rice, beans, yam, and fish', the word 'yam' usually takes
questions.explanation: Items before the last in a list rise; only the final item 'fish' falls.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: The final item in a list usually takes what intonation?
questions.explanation: The last item of a list completes the thought and takes a falling tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: Which sentence takes a FALLING intonation at the end?
questions.explanation: The command 'Close the door' is said with falling intonation; the others rise.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Intonation
questions.q: In expressing strong surprise ('You PASSED the exam!'), we usually use
questions.explanation: Strong surprise raises the pitch, so the exclamation ends with a rising tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is 'ea' pronounced /iː/?
questions.explanation: Meat is /miːt/; in bread, head and dead the 'ea' is /e/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is 'ea' pronounced /e/?
questions.explanation: Bread is /bred/ with /e/; meat /miːt/, sea /siː/ and team /tiːm/ have /iː/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'a' pronounced /eɪ/?
questions.explanation: Name is /neɪm/ with /eɪ/; man /mæn/ and map /mæp/ have /æ/, and make uses the 'a-e' pattern.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'y' pronounced /aɪ/?
questions.explanation: My is /maɪ/ with /aɪ/ for 'y'; in yes and yellow it is /j/, and in system it is /ɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is 'ou' pronounced /ʌ/?
questions.explanation: Country is /ˈkʌntri/ with /ʌ/; house /haʊs/, mouth /maʊθ/ and loud /laʊd/ use /aʊ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is 'oo' pronounced /ʊ/?
questions.explanation: Good is /ɡʊd/ with the short /ʊ/; the others all have the long /uː/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is 'oo' pronounced /ʌ/?
questions.explanation: Blood is /blʌd/ with /ʌ/; good /ɡʊd/, boot /buːt/ and food /fuːd/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'o' pronounced /əʊ/?
questions.explanation: Go is /gəʊ/ with /əʊ/; hot /hɒt/, lock /lɒk/ and box /bɒks/ have /ɒ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the final 'e' silent?
questions.explanation: Made is /meɪd/ and the final 'e' is not pronounced; in the others the 'e' is heard.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'c' pronounced /k/?
questions.explanation: Car is /kɑː/; in city, magic and special the 'c' sounds as /s/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Homophones
questions.q: Which pair of words are homophones?
questions.explanation: Rain /reɪn/ and reign /reɪn/ sound the same but differ in meaning and spelling.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Homophones
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of words are homophones?
questions.explanation: Flower /ˈflaə/ and flour /ˈflaʊə/ are pronounced identically.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Homophones
questions.q: Which pair of words below are homophones?
questions.explanation: Meet /miːt/ and meat /miːt/ are pronounced the same.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Homophones
questions.q: Which of these pairs of words are homophones?
questions.explanation: Know /nəʊ/ and no /nəʊ/ are pronounced the same; now /naʊ/, nose /nəʊz/ and not /nɒt/ differ.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Homophones
questions.q: Which pair of words is pronounced exactly the same?
questions.explanation: Hear /hɪə/ and here /hɪə/ sound the same in Nigerian English.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Homophones
questions.q: Which two words sound exactly alike?
questions.explanation: To /tuː/ and two /tuː/ are pronounced identically.
